correctness.rationale: For every m≥2 over C, r=2m+1, the highest order-(r−1) transvectant gives three quadratic equations defining the codimension-three complete-intersection quadratic hull (Massri known premise). The odd-degree invariant alternating SL2 form yields the quadratic moment map dμ_f(e)(ξ)=ω(ξf,e), so Jacobian rank equals SL2-orbit dimension. Semisimple Lie elements have only nonzero odd weights; nilpotent stabilizers occur precisely at pure powers, giving exact reduced singular support C_r. At a0=1 choose the a1 orbit slice, eliminate a_(r−1),a_r with two unit linear pivots, and let t=a2, z=a3..a_(r−2). The antidiagonal Hessian of the residual at t=0 is nonsingular. Parametric holomorphic Morse reduction and positive weighted equivariance force h(t)=c t^(m+1); c≠0 since c=0 produces a second singular-support dimension, contradicting the global rank computation. The germ is A1 × {sum_(2m−3) z_i²+t^(m+1)=0}; Jacobian transverse quotient has length m. Uniform argument is analytic, not inferred from finite samples.

value.rationale: A natural stable family of binary-form osculating quadratic hulls receives an exact singular-support classification and transverse analytic ADE type, together with scheme-theoretic Jacobian multiplicity m. These structural invariants are not determined by codimension, degree or a known inclusion of C_r in the singular locus, and identify all singularities uniformly for m≥2. A future algebraic geometer could use the precise transverse type and length when studying resolutions and singular schemes.

limitations: Only odd binary degree ≥5 over C with complex-analytic local germs; does not identify a globally trivial neighborhood or even-degree hulls. Exact analytic type rests on known complete-intersection premise, not independently reproving every earlier external theorem.
